security_audit.summary: All 21 static Ruby/shell backtick findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline filename examples, formulas, tables, and slash command references in SKILL.md. No shell or Ruby execution instructions, prompt injection, or data exfiltration intent were found. The only net-new issue is overbroad declared tool access, because Bash is allowed even though the financial modeling workflow does not require shell execution.

remediation.issue: Bash is included in allowed-tools without documented need.
remediation.suggestion: Remove Bash from allowed-tools, or add a clear and narrow justification for any required shell use.

remediation.issue: Network tools are broadly declared for a planning workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Use WebSearch and WebFetch only for explicit user-approved benchmark research, and document that scope in the skill.

content.value_statement: Startup founders need credible projections for planning, hiring, and fundraising. This skill structures assumptions into revenue, cost, headcount, cash flow, and scenario analysis.
actual_capabilities: Collects business model, pricing, customer, cash, growth, cost, and funding assumptions.
Builds cohort-based revenue projections with retention, ARPU, expansion revenue, and growth cadence.
Models COGS, sales, marketing, research, development, administration, and fully loaded headcount costs.
Calculates cash flow, burn rate, runway, CAC, LTV, burn multiple, and efficiency metrics.
Creates conservative, base, and optimistic scenarios for fundraising and operating plans.
Produces a structured markdown report with assumptions, metrics, risks, and validation checks.
limitations: Projection quality depends on the accuracy of user-provided assumptions and current business data.
It does not replace professional accounting, tax, legal, or investment advice.
It produces markdown planning output, not a native spreadsheet workbook.
Market benchmarks and compensation data should be verified for the company stage and region.

use_cases.title: Prepare Fundraising Projections
use_cases.description: Create a credible financial model with revenue, burn, runway, and funding milestones for investor discussions.

use_cases.title: Plan Hiring and Budget Needs
use_cases.description: Translate growth targets into department budgets, hiring plans, fully loaded costs, and cash requirements.

use_cases.title: Review Scenario Risk
use_cases.description: Compare conservative, base, and optimistic cases to understand runway sensitivity and operating tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Projection
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a three-year financial projection for my startup. Ask me for the inputs you need before building the model.

prompt_templates.title: Build a SaaS Revenue Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a SaaS revenue model using MRR, ARPU, churn, new customers, expansion revenue, and gross margin assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Model Cash and Hiring
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a headcount, cost, burn, and runway plan for the next 36 months using my growth and funding assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Stress Test Fundraising Scenarios
prompt_templates.prompt: Build conservative, base, and optimistic scenarios, then identify funding needs, key risks, and metrics investors will question.

output_examples.input: A B2B SaaS startup has 100 customers, 50,000 dollars MRR, 10 percent monthly churn, and 500,000 dollars cash.
output: A three-year revenue projection with monthly detail for the first two years.
A cash runway view showing burn rate, hiring costs, and funding timing.
A metrics summary with CAC, LTV, burn multiple, and scenario comparisons.

output_examples.input: A marketplace startup needs a fundraising model for a seed round and wants conservative, base, and optimistic cases.
output: Scenario assumptions for customer growth, take rate, churn, CAC, and operating expenses.
Funding requirement estimates linked to hiring milestones and runway targets.
Validation notes that highlight sensitive assumptions and investor review questions.

output_examples.input: A finance lead wants to update projections after actual revenue and hiring results changed this quarter.
output: A refreshed planning summary that compares actuals against prior assumptions.
Updated cash flow, runway, and headcount plans for leadership review.
A list of assumptions to monitor during the next monthly planning cycle.

best_practices: Provide current revenue, customer, cash, churn, pricing, and team data before asking for a full model.
Use separate conservative, base, and optimistic assumptions instead of changing only the final revenue target.
Review the output with finance, legal, and accounting experts before using it for investor materials.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the model as a guaranteed forecast or investment recommendation.
Do not hide weak assumptions, missing cost categories, or aggressive growth rates.
Do not use stale benchmarks when compensation, CAC, pricing, or market conditions have changed.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a structured financial projection report covering revenue, costs, headcount, cash flow, metrics, and scenarios.

faq.question: Which business models does it support?
faq.answer: It supports SaaS, marketplace, transaction, e-commerce, and other models when the user provides suitable assumptions.

faq.question: Does it create an Excel file?
faq.answer: No. It creates markdown planning output and can provide formulas for conversion into a spreadsheet.

faq.question: Can it help with fundraising?
faq.answer: Yes. It can estimate funding needs, runway, use of proceeds, milestones, and investor-facing metrics.

faq.question: How accurate are the projections?
faq.answer: Accuracy depends on the quality of assumptions, current data, market benchmarks, and regular updates against actual results.

faq.question: Should investors rely on this output alone?
faq.answer: No. Founders should review the model with qualified finance, accounting, legal, and tax professionals.
